description: Exergy-based and economic comparison of Claude, Heylandt and Kapitza liquefaction cycles for cryogenic energy storage, with and without cold storage. 18 pages.
attribution: Hamdy, S.; Moser, T.; Morosuk, T.; Tsatsaronis, G. Exergy-Based and Economic Evaluation of Liquefaction Processes for Cryogenics Energy Storage. Energies 2019, 12, 493. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
notes: Stored because it isolates the single biggest variable in the liquefaction literature: cold recycle reduces specific power by 50-70%, which is why quoted figures range from 263 to 880 kWh per tonne for the same processes. An airborne plant making nitrogen from ambient air has no discharge cycle returning cold to it, so the upper half of that range is the relevant one and our 450 kWh per tonne sits below it.
